items.title: Houthis claim Saudi strikes killed 33 in Yemen, including 13 children
items.summary: SANAA: Houthi authorities said on Sunday that Saudi strikes killed 33 people, many of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as deaths mount in the country's revived civil war. The death toll from the Saudi-led coalition's strikes on Al-Shariya village located east of Yemen's capital Sanaa has risen to 33, with 39 people wounded, Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi said in a post on X. "According to the near-final figures, the dead include 12 men, 8 women and 13 children, while the injured include 16 men, 10 women and 13 children," Alasbahi said.

items.title: RM1,000 lifeline: Sabah taxi drivers get first-ever cash aid as passengers dwindle
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 8 — The one-off RM1,000 Special Financial Assistance under Budget 2027 has come as a relief to taxi drivers in Sabah, whose daily earnings have dwindled amid growing competition from other modes of transport. Azizarjan Japar, 43, a mother of four, said competition from newer transport services had left many conventional taxi drivers going entire days without picking up a single passenger. She said the cash assistance would also provide some financial breathing space for women drivers like herself as they grappled with the rising cost of living.

items.title: Qiulae Wong, the outsider who could decide New Zealand's next government
items.summary: That would mean either a centre-right or centre-left bloc would require the support of Wong's centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time. Opportunity's flagship policies centre on tax, with an annual NZ$19,400 (US$10,800) universal basic income for most New Zealand residents funded by a 1.75 per cent annual land tax. The party also wants to simplify the country's income tax system.

items.title: New Zealand preliminary vote leaves unclear who will govern
items.summary: Electoral Commission preliminary results showed coalition partners National, ACT and New Zealand First with 67 of the currently projected 131-seat parliament. Sixty-six seats are needed for a majority. However, the commission said special votes, around 14 per cent of the total vote, still need to be counted.

items.title: Smart budgeting strategies strengthen financial resilience
items.summary: LETTER: Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent provides some reassurance to Malaysian households, offering greater certainty in financial planning as families prepare for the year-end holidays. However, an unchanged OPR does not mean that living costs will remain unchanged. As the year draws to a close, many families are planning their school holiday trips.

items.title: KTMB equipment storage facility destroyed in Sepang fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) storage facility in Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, was 95 per cent destroyed in a fire last night. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.42pm, with the first fire engine arriving at the scene at 11pm. "The fire was already raging when firefighters arrived.

items.title: Ships, defence and halal: What Zahid discussed with Turkiye’s consul in Bursa
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — The potential to develop a ship maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) hub in Bagan Datuk, Perak, was among the main topics discussed at a meeting between Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysia’s Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer, here yesterday. At the 30-minute meeting, which began at 11am local time (4pm in Malaysia), Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia had domestic shipping industry capabilities and had attracted interest from foreign investors seeking opportunities in Bagan Datuk, with participation from Turkiye among those receiving attention. Ahmad Zahid said the meeting also covered opportunities for transferring Turkiye’s technological expertise, building local industrial capacity and expanding cooperation in high-value sectors with the potential to benefit both countries’ economies.

items.title: Residents urge installation of traffic lights at high-risk Jalan Slim junction
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM: Residents near Perumahan Awam 3, Jalan Slim Lama here, are calling for urgent action to install traffic lights at a junction linking the Behrang Stesen-Tanjung Malim Highway (FT193) and Jalan Slim-Behrang Ulu (A121), where they claim frequent crashes, including fatal cases, have occurred. Yameeun Marsudi, 75, who has lived in the area since 1996, said traffic lights were urgently needed to regulate traffic flow and reduce the risk of collisions between vehicles. "Every time road users want to head towards Jalan Slim or make a U-turn to enter Perumahan Awam 3, navigating this junction feels like risking their lives.

items.title: Heavy rain floods parts of Central Seberang Perai, fallen trees hit cars and homes
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 8 — Heavy rain yesterday evening has caused flooding in several areas in Central Seberang Perai, while two separate incidents involving fallen trees damaged vehicles and part of a building structure in the district. The Central Seberang Perai District Disaster Management Committee secretariat said the affected areas included Seberang Jaya, Permatang Rawa, Tanah Liat, Mengkuang Titi and Jalan Baru, following heavy rain that began at about 4.30pm. It said several homes were also affected by rising water, while drainage problems were reported around Seberang Jaya, although the situation remained under control.

items.title: Police round up nine suspects after 19-year-old killed in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 8 — Police have detained nine individuals aged between 16 and 42 to assist in investigations into the murder of a 19-year-old who is believed to have been stabbed during a fight at a public park in Jalan Gambir here early yesterday. Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said all suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm today following intelligence gathering and investigations by the Sibu District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department (CID). Abang Zainal Abidin added that the incident had also gone viral on Facebook.

items.title: Melaka polls: Adam Adli urges young voters to make fact-based decisions, not be swayed by sentiment
items.summary: MELAKA: Young voters in the state have been urged to exercise their voting power in the 16th Melaka state election by making informed decisions based on accurate information and facts. Melaka PKR state leadership council acting chairman, Adam Adli Abd Halim, said they should not be influenced by sentiment or politics of hate when casting their ballots on Nov 14. Adam Adli said he was optimistic about Melaka's future after witnessing the active participation of the state's younger generation in the democratic process.

items.title: Two women injured in Brickfields restaurant fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two women were injured, one of whom suffered a fractured left arm, in a fire involving two double-storey restaurant premises along Jalan Tun Sambanthan in Brickfields early this morning. Operations commander Md Fuad Selamat said the Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 3.04am, with firemen arriving at the scene four minutes later. "The fire completely destroyed the ground floor and damaged 50 per cent of the upper floor," he said in a statement.

items.title: Fahmi joins two ministerial-level Doha forums to strengthen global digital cooperation
items.summary: DOHA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil is scheduled to take part in two ministerial-level forums today focusing on strengthening international cooperation in the development and future of the digital ecosystem. The two events are the Ministerial Panel at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026: Digital Leadership Forum and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) Ministerial Roundtable, both taking place at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre (DECC). According to the official programme of the Malaysian delegation, Fahmi is scheduled to attend the MWC Doha 2026 welcome ceremony before joining a ministerial panel session titled "Accelerating Cooperation for a Connected Digital Future".

items.title: Two hours of rain, one closed bridge: Subang’s Kampung Melayu hit by flash floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Heavy rain that lasted for about two hours caused flash flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang and Jalan Jati Bridge that spans Sungai Damansara has been closed due to erosion along the riverbank. Meanwhile, the Selangor Public Works Department (JKR), in a separate statement, said the Jalan Jati Bridge in Section U6, Kampung Melayu Subang, had been closed to all vehicles for safety reasons following severe erosion of the bridge abutment structure. According to the department, the erosion and embankment collapse occurred following a rise in water levels and strong currents in Sungai Damansara due to continuous heavy rain.

items.title: #NSTviral: Batu Caves fireworks display lights up social media [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A spectacular fireworks display over Batu Caves and surrounding areas last night has gone viral on social media, drawing thousands of reactions on Threads. As the Indian community in Malaysia welcomed Deepavali, a two-minute-and-52-second video captured a dazzling display of fireworks illuminating the night sky, accompanied by a continuous rumble of explosions. Happy Deepavali."

items.title: Ringgit expected to trade with slight positive bias next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade with a slight positive bias against the US dollar next week as investors assess the outlook for the US interest rates. "Softer inflation readings could weigh on US Treasury yields and the greenback, providing support for the ringgit. "Therefore, next week the ringgit is expected to trade within RM4.04-RM4.06 against the US dollar," he said.

items.title: Ministers, deputy ministers send Deepavali wishes, urge Malaysians to keep unity strong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Several ministers have extended Deepavali greetings to those celebrating, calling on the public to preserve unity, harmony, and wellbeing. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek expressed hope that the meaningful festival would offer families an opportunity to spend quality time together and strengthen familial bonds. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the festive season is an ideal platform for mutual visits and fostering ties across ethnic and cultural lines.

items.title: Mara to double number of students sent to Turkiye next year
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move was part of efforts to strengthen academic ties between the two countries. "I will ensure that, at the very least, Mara will send twice the number of students to the same university next year," he said at a dinner with Malaysian students and Malaysian Embassy staff in Turkiye last night. Meanwhile, Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision to send the 17 students followed discussions with the Turkish government that began in April.

items.title: Tiong: M'sia's international safety image key to tourist confidence
items.summary: SIBU: Malaysia's international safety image must be given due attention as it influences foreign tourists' confidence in visiting the country, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said. We must find ways to address the people's problems," he said at the 2026 Navy Veterans Samudera Heritage Charity Gala Dinner here last night. The event was organised by the Sarawak branch of the Royal Malaysian Navy Veterans Association (PVTLDM).

items.title: Bursa Malaysia expected to trade within 1,600-1,630 range next week
items.summary: On the index board, the FBM Emas Index slipped 96.26 points to 11,965.47, the FBM Top 100 Index decreased 65.41 points to 11,798.45, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index sank 260.14 points to 11,822.77. The FBM ACE Index lost 163.67 points to 5,240.24 and the FBM Mid 70 Index tumbled 399.81 points to 17,020.88. Weekly turnover narrowed to 15.49 billion units worth RM14.43 billion from 15.53 billion units worth RM9.97 billion in the previous week.

items.title: Flags, ceramah and festive lights: Melaka juggles polls and Deepavali
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Amid the fervour of the 16th Melaka State Election campaign, filled with political ceramah and party flags, the atmosphere in the historic city centre eased briefly as it was illuminated by Deepavali festivities last night. Members of the Indian community shop for last-minute Deepavali essentials at Little India in Melaka City on November 7, 2026. More news on the 16th Melaka State Election at https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026.

items.title: Melaka polls: Young voters crucial to BN's election hopes
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional is focusing on young voters in its bid to win the Melaka election, recognising their potential to account for a significant share of the total votes. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said young voters were the future leaders of the country and had an important role in determining the state's direction. "Young voters are being prepared to become future leaders.

items.title: 20 injured as 5.7-magnitude earthquake strikes central Japan
items.summary: TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.7 struck central Japan early today, injuring at least 20 people in Aichi Prefecture. The 1.04am tremor originated in western Shizuoka Prefecture at a depth of about 40 kilometres and registered upper 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale in Chita, Aichi Prefecture, the Japan Meteorological Agency said. In Aichi Prefecture, the fire department reported that two people in Toyota City were likely injured.

items.title: Dashcam footage? Police seek witnesses after couple from Cheras die in North-South Highway skid
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 8 — An elderly couple died after the car they were travelling in skidded into a drain at KM242 of the southbound North-South Expressway (PLUS) here this afternoon. Rembau District Police Chief Supt Ngiam Ooi Ming said the 75-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, while his 70-year-old wife died while receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital at about 8 pm. Without disclosing the victims’ names in the statement, he said the female passenger was seriously injured and receiving treatment at Rembau Hospital, while the driver was unhurt.

items.title: M'sian diaspora in Qatar conducts evacuation drills for war threats
items.summary: DOHA, (Qatar): The Malaysian diaspora in Qatar is taking proactive steps to strengthen emergency preparedness by conducting evacuation drills, including simulations involving war and nuclear threats. Malaysian Ambassador to Qatar Faizal Razali said the initiatives, organised by the Malaysian community through the Malaysian Association in Qatar (MAQ), also involved Malaysians in Bahrain as part of preparations for possible security crises in the region. Faizal said MAQ also organised various interactive activities, including talks and online concerts, to help ease the anxiety of Malaysians during crises.

items.title: Clashes erupt in Paris as thousands join fresh protests across France
items.summary: PARIS: Thousands of people protested across France Saturday in a new show of anger against the government with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than on previous weeks. A total of 146,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said. At the end of the protest in Paris, police used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles and homemade fireworks at the security forces, an AFP correspondent said.

items.title: Iran claims its forces are 'stronger' than at start of war
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran said on Saturday its military had grown stronger since the outset of the war with the United States, as mediators including Qatar worked to prevent any return to fighting after months of deadlock in the conflict. Washington also offered a US$20 million reward for information about Teheran's nuclear programme. US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.

items.title: Eisenkot tasked with forming government in bid to oust Netanyahu
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's president announced on Saturday he would task Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following last week's election, in what Netanyahu's rivals see as a first step to remove the country's longest-serving prime minister. President Isaac Herzog said that after consultations with all parties during the week, he would grant Eisenkot the first chance to form a government after the Oct 27 election, in which neither side secured a majority in a country deeply polarised by Netanyahu's hard-right rule and worn down by three years of war. Eisenkot, who later pledged to "do everything" to form a new government, was recommended by parties representing 67 lawmakers as opposed to 46 for Netanyahu's bloc.

items.title: Trump asks Justice Department to investigate Democrats over impeachment threats
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration. Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. "The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

items.title: Eat, mingle, celebrate: Five Deepavali open houses from Brickfields to Ipoh for all Malaysians
items.summary: But there is also one truly Malaysian tradition to fete every major festival here — the open house. An open house is not just an elaborate feast. National Deepavali Celebration, Brickfields — November 14 One of the biggest open houses will be the National Deepavali Celebration, organised by the National Unity Ministry in the Little India enclave of Brickfields on November 14.

items.title: Gunman 'fascinated by far-right' kills six in Poland
items.summary: Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the gunman appeared to be "fascinated by far-right ideologies." "Two people who have not yet been identified," Boron said referring to the victims killed. The suspect – a Polish citizen born in 2002 – drove a car onto Krakow's Main Market Square and began shooting at random people, said police.

items.title: King Charles open to China visit, but palace says it would be carefully considered
items.summary: LONDON: A British monarch has only ever made one state visit to China: Queen Elizabeth II four decades ago. King Charles III would consider undertaking the second, according to an aide. "If the government said, 'Will the king go to China?'

items.title: Pope Leo condemns violence, child deaths in Uruguay's crime-hit neighbourhood
items.summary: MONTEVIDEO: Pope Leo XIV on Saturday slammed the deaths of children in areas of wealthy Uruguay gripped by drug violence, as he visited the most crime-ridden neighborhood in the South American country. Leo walked amid high security through the streets of the Casavalle area of Montevideo, where the murder rate is four times the national average. "There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home," the pope said.

items.title: Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was offering a press secretary role to mixed martial arts executive and "violent fighter" Dana White. While White did not explicitly accept the job, the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss posted a photo – possibly AI-generated – that showed him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned "On to the next chapter." Trump also listed six UFC fighters that he hoped White would bring to the White House as advisers, "even though some are not from our Country."

items.title: Gardenia probes complaints over products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd is investigating complaints from consumers following claims on social media that several children had fallen ill after consuming its products. The company said it took the reports seriously and was concerned about the well-being of the consumers and families involved. "Gardenia KL is committed to providing safe and high-quality products to our consumers," it said.

items.title: Elderly couple killed after car skids into drain on Plus Highway
items.summary: SEREMBAN: An elderly couple died after the car they were travelling in skidded into a drain at KM242 of the southbound North-South Expressway (PLUS) Saturday afternoon. Rembau police chief Superintendent Ngiam Ooi Ming said the 75-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, while his 70-year-old wife died while receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital at 8pm. Ngiam said the female passenger was seriously injured and receiving treatment at Rembau Hospital, while the driver was unhurt.

items.title: Five killed in shooting in main square of Polish city of Krakow
items.summary: WARSAW: Five people have died and more than 10 have been injured in a shooting on the main market square in Krakow, police said on Saturday. "The perpetrator was shot by police officers and is currently being transported to a hospital," police wrote on X. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Cabinet ministers, state leaders extend Deepavali wishes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Several cabinet ministers have extended Deepavali greetings to those celebrating, calling on the public to preserve unity, harmony, and wellbeing. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek expressed hope that the meaningful festival would offer families an opportunity to spend quality time together and strengthen familial bonds. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the festive season is an ideal platform for mutual visits and fostering ties across ethnic and cultural lines.

items.title: More than new clothes and sweets, Deepavali is about family and tradition
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 7 — Deepavali celebrations are not just about wearing new attire and preparing an array of traditional delicacies, but also about strengthening family bonds and preserving age-old traditions passed down through generations. For Singaporean P. Parvathy, 65, from Sengkang, a visit to Johor Bahru to shop for Deepavali essentials has become an annual tradition, while also giving her the opportunity to meet relatives living in the state. She said her visit to the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Ungku Puan here also allowed her to browse a variety of decorative items for the home, including floral ornaments to hang at the entrance, traditional attire and bangles.

items.title: This Deepavali, Anwar calls on Malaysians to celebrate differences and shared values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need. Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal ! (Deepavali greetings),” he added.

items.title: After deadly Paya Terubong landslide, Chow says DOSH must finish probe first
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang state government will decide whether to set up a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) into the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong once the state Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) completes its investigation and submits its findings and recommendations. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would await the findings of the DOSH investigation before considering further action over the incident, which claimed the life of a 73-year-old doctor. “DOSH is conducting its investigation and will provide recommendations (to the state government) once it is completed.

items.title: Zahid says Malaysia stands ready to help Lebanon rebuild after conflict
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia is ready to help Lebanon rebuild following the conflict that has affected the country, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. “Malaysia and Lebanon share a special friendship, particularly through Malaysia’s involvement in peacekeeping operations under the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) since 2007. Insya-Allah,” he said.

items.title: Najib’s lawyers seek immediate transfer home, say King’s decree must be executed today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Lawyers for Datuk Seri Najib Razak are contesting the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) decision to temporarily suspend his house arrest, demanding the former prime minister be transferred to his home immediately. In a media statement today, the legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co. argued that the AGC’s “temporary suspension” of the house arrest order contradicts the King’s explicit decree issued this morning. The statement noted that the AGC issued a subsequent media statement 57 minutes after the King’s decree, which did not reference the royal order.

items.title: Penang sets aside RM4.5m to grow startups, AI adoption and digital economy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang government has allocated RM4.5 million in its 2027 budget to support technology startups, accelerate digitalisation among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and expand the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across the state’s economy. “In (the state’s) Budget 2027, the state government has set aside RM4.5 million for Digital Penang; it will support technology start-ups, help small and medium enterprises go digital, and use AI across our economy. Also present at the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 were chairman Lukas J.Tan and SEGi College Penang head of student experience Vincent Tung Chin Aun.

items.title: Nancy wants 42,000 men to seek health support and join family decisions
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is targeting 42,000 men to benefit from government-provided well-being services for men, as part of efforts to raise awareness of the importance of healthcare among them. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the initiative also encouraged men to seek relevant health information and services with their partners, particularly when making decisions about family health. She was speaking at the November National Family Month 2026 celebration, which was launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and attended by his wife, Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, and Selangor State Executive Councillor for Women and Community Welfare Anfaal Saari.

items.title: All eyes on Nov 14 as police strengthen readiness for Melaka vote
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is strengthening its level of preparedness to ensure public safety and order are maintained throughout the 16th Melaka State Election, which will be held on Nov 14. According to a post on the Melaka Police Facebook page, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, in his address during a working visit to the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) yesterday, touched on several matters, including duty assignment, security management and the responsibilities of every personnel in ensuring the smooth conduct of the election process. According to the post, Mohd Khalid also reminded PDRM personnel to safeguard the confidentiality of official information, strengthen esprit de corps and ensure compliance with the chain of command and control to guarantee the effectiveness of every assignment.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution wants schools, police and health authorities to share data on at-risk students
items.summary: KULIM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), the Ministry of Education (MOE), and the Ministry of Health (MOH) must strengthen their cooperation and information-sharing to address various security issues and create a safe school ecosystem. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said these three ministries cannot work in isolation when dealing with the various issues that arise within schools. Saifuddin Nasution emphasised that collaboration among the three ministries is crucial, given that the school security ecosystem encompasses approximately 5.2 million students across 12,000 schools nationwide, a situation that necessitates information-sharing and integrated action among the relevant agencies.

items.title: Two step-sisters killed after car skids and crashes on PLUS highway near Tanjong Malim
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 7 — Two step-siblings died when the vehicle they were in skidded in an accident at Kilometre 388 of the North-South Expressway (Plus) southbound, near Tanjong Malim today. Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said an 18-year-old girl was pronounced dead at the scene, while a six-year-old girl who suffered severe injuries died while receiving treatment at the Slim River Hospital. Earlier, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Tanjong Malim Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call regarding the accident at 8.35am.

items.title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 7 — The country’s online banking system and financial transactions remain secure despite attempted cyberattacks by non-state actors, including a recent hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Communications Minister and Madani government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the hacking attempts detected so far had not resulted in data theft or affected the country’s online banking operations. On the hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Fahmi said it was confined to changes to the website’s appearance and involved a third-party-managed site.

items.title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak nearly triple to over 4,000 in hours
items.summary: In SELANGOR , the number of flood evacuees still sheltering at PPS this afternoon rose to 3,798 from 128 families at two centres, compared with 1,206 from 316 families at nine centres this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, PPS Sekolah Agama Batu Lapan Ijok is sheltering 2,999 evacuees from 67 families, while 799 evacuees from 61 families are at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang. Meanwhile, in PERAK , the number of flood and storm evacuees rose to 270 from 79 families this afternoon, compared with 198 from 58 families this morning, across the Hilir Perak and Manjung districts.

items.title: AG seeks audience with King to clarify Najib’s house arrest issue, says Anwar
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has requested an audience with His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in his SRC International case, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. “I have asked for the Attorney General to immediately meet the Agong to ‘ mohon ampun ’ (apologise) and explain why that decision was accepted for the SRC case, but there is a problem as it involves the second case, which is the 1MDB case. Earlier, Anwar said he wanted to avoid this house arrest matter from becoming politicised.

items.title: Bukit Aman suspects cocaine-in-shoes arrest at Hong Kong airport linked to Malaysia drug bust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The arrest of a Hong Kong man with about one kilogramme of cocaine concealed in his shoes at Hong Kong International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur last Wednesday is believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate recently crippled by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). “We believe the syndicate has been crippled following the arrest of a Hong Kong national believed to be the syndicate leader and a local recruiter, as announced at yesterday’s press conference,” he said when contacted today. Media reports today said a 36-year-old Hong Kong man was arrested last Wednesday after customs officers found cocaine estimated to be worth HK$600,000 (RM311,000) during an inspection at Hong Kong International Airport following his arrival from Malaysia.

items.title: Tourism Ministry open to helping international event organisers facing funding challenges, says Tiong
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) is prepared to consider collaborating with and providing assistance to organisers of international events in Malaysia, particularly those facing financial constraints. Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said the move was aimed at encouraging more international events to be held in the country while attracting greater participation from overseas. Tiong said the ministry would also explore possible forms of collaboration and assistance to help organisers address their financial challenges.

items.title: DAP yet to discuss replacing Anthony Loke as transport minister, says party vice-chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — DAP has yet to discuss a replacement for Transport Minister Anthony Loke, whose resignation remains conditional on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returning home to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. DAP vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan said discussions about a potential successor would be premature because Loke’s resignation had not taken effect, the New Straits Times reported. Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, reaffirmed yesterday that his resignation would take effect only when Najib physically returned home to begin serving his sentence under house arrest.

items.title: Teenager, 19, dies after being stabbed during alleged argument at Sibu park
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 7 — A 19-year-old youth died after being stabbed in the chest during an incident at a public park along Jalan Gambir here around midnight last night. It is understood that nearby residents heard a woman screaming from the direction of the park, prompting them to alert the police. When contacted today, Sibu District Police Chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad confirmed that the case was still under investigation.

items.title: Security presence disappears from Najib’s Taman Duta residence as house arrest remains on hold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The security presence outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence was nowhere to be seen today, a day after the Taman Duta property was placed under tight security ahead of his anticipated return under house arrest. The heightened security came as preparations were made for Najib’s expected return after he paid a RM50 million fine in the SRC International corruption case, fulfilling a key condition of a royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028. Despite the absence of security personnel today, local and international journalists remained stationed near the residence, awaiting further developments.

items.title: Integrity must go hand in hand with academic success, Perlis Raja Muda tells UniSIRAJ graduates
items.summary: Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, who is also UniSIRAJ Chancellor, said knowledge developed one’s ability to think and solve problems, while good manners reflected one’s values. “Ensure that academic excellence and expertise are always accompanied by strong moral values and principles,” he said at the 9th UniSIRAJ Convocation Ceremony at Dewan 2020 here today. Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said that in an era of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital advancement, the pursuit of knowledge must always go hand in hand with noble values and strong principles.

items.title: The journey home begins: Deepavali rush brings slow traffic to major highways across Malaysia
items.summary: “Traffic was also slow at the Johor Causeway, from Woodlands Checkpoint (CIQ) in Singapore to Sultan Iskandar CIQ in Johor in the northbound direction, while congestion was reported on the Second Link Expressway, from the Second Link Bridge to Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ in Johor, also northbound,” they said when contacted today. Traffic volume had also increased on the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE), affecting the northbound stretches from Gamuda Cove to Bandar Saujana Putra and Putra Heights to Shah Alam, as well as the southbound stretch from Putra Heights to Gamuda Cove. Meanwhile, on the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), traffic was slow on the northbound stretches from Bandar Tasik Selatan to Kuchai and Serdang to Pekan Sungai Besi.

items.title: Umno leaders lodge police reports, Dr Akmal demands action on Najib’s house arrest delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Several Umno leaders in Johor have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest, as Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh called for similar reports to be filed nationwide. Pontian Umno chief Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, who is also a party supreme council member, lodged the report at the Benut police station at 12.30pm today, accompanied by his deputy Mohd Sumali Reduan, division vice-chief Jamaludin Abd Majid and several grassroots leaders. “A police report was lodged over the delay in implementing the house arrest order for Najib, which should have been carried out,” Ahmad said in a Facebook post.
